INTRODUCTIONM

Conventional vacuum tubes and LC tank circuits cannot be used.
Special types of vacuum tubes and special components are used at microwave frequencies.

Cavity resonators are microwave devices that perform the function of a parallel LC circuit.
DISCUSSION
They are used in place of a capacitor and inductor in microwave circuits.
For example, a cavity resonator can be used as the tank circuit in an oscillator to determine frequency.
Conventional components are not used because they cannot be manufactured with small enough values to produce the high microwave frequencies.

How cavity resonators operate is best described as placing an infinite number of shorted quarter wave transmission lines together. Let's see why.
By shorting a transmission line, the line becomes a parallel LC circuit.
The values of L and C are extremely small making the resonant frequency extremely high.
The frequency at which the circuit becomes resonant is determined by where the shorting bar is placed.
Placing the shorting bar at a distance that equals one quarter wave length of the desired frequency produces a resonant circuit.

Electron transit time is the time for electrons to travel from the cathode to the plate.
Transit time causes phase shifts between grid voltage and plate current. Power losses can be high.
For efficient vacuum tube operation, the grid voltage and plate current must be in phase and the power losses have to be low.
For example, a transit time of .5 nanoseconds between the grid and plate is only .0000005 cycles at 1 kHz.
For example, a transit time of .5 nanoseconds between the grid and plate is only .0000005 cycles at 1 kHz.
TRANSIT TIME CYCLES - A signal that is 1 kHz has a period of 1millisecond. A transit time of .5 nanoseconds is only 2/1,000,000 of the time for one cycle or .0000005 cycles.
There is effectively no phase shift between the grid and plate or power loss through the grid.
At 1 MHz, a .5 nanosecond transit time is .0005 cycles. Again, there is no phase shift or power loss.
However, at 1 GHz, a .5 nanosecond transit time is .5 cycles or one half cycle.
This is a 180 degree phase shift between the grid voltage and plate current. Also, because of the phase shift there is a power loss through the grid.

As you have seen, normal vacuum tubes are not efficient at microwave frequencies.
If you try to decrease interelectrode capacitance by increasing the spacing between the elements, you increase the transit time.
If you decrease the size of the tube to decrease interelectrode capacitance and lead inductance, you lower the power handling capabilities.
For these reasons, special microwave tubes were developed.
A Klystron tube is capable of operating as an amplifier, oscillator or mixer.
The frequency range is between 800 MHz and 30 GHz. The basic operation is as follows.

A filament, cathode and accelerating grid produce a stream of electrons that travel along the tube toward a collector plate. Along the way they pass a cavity called the buncher cavity, which is connected to a pair of grids...
The buncher cavity is constructed in such a way as to act as a tuned circuit, with the AC (RF) input signal coming in and being applied to the pair of grids, which are connected to the cavity.
As the first grid becomes positive and the second becomes negative, the electrons approaching the cavity are accelerated forward by the first grid. signal.
The electrons are first accelerated into the grid space by the positive first grid and are then slowed by the negatively charged second grid. grid. signal.

As the input changes polarity, the grids also change polarity. Now the electrons that are between the grids are accelerated forward by the (now positive) second grid, while the electrons approaching the (now negative) first grid are slowed by its charge..

Then the signal's polarity again reverses, and the process repeats. The result is that the electron stream has been turned into a series of clusters (or bunches) of electrons. The distance which separates the bunches corresponds to the frequency of the original input signal....

Keep in mind that the amount of acceleration or deceleration that the electrons experience is dependent on two things: their relative distances from the charged grids and the varying amount of charge on the grids.
VELOCITY MODULATION - Modification of an electron stream by an alternate acceleration and deceleration of the electrons with a period comparable to that of the transit time in the space concerned...

As the electrons pass through these grids, they give up much of their energy through inductance. This energy is then passed from the catcher grids to the catcher cavity which, like the buncher cavity, is a tuned cavity...

A magnetron tube is primarily used as a high power microwave oscillator in the frequency range of 1 to 5 GHz.
It is basically a diode that operates using both electric and magnetic fields. The basic operation is as follows.
The cathode, directly or indirectly heated, emits electrons that are attracted to the anode, which has a very high positive potential.
The anode is a solid piece of metal that has a large hole drilled in the middle for the cathode.
Smaller holes drilled around the outer edges are used as cavity resonators...ors.
At this time, the electrons leave the cathode and flow to the anode. No oscillations are developed.
By adding a strong magnet around the tube, the path of the electrons from the cathode to the anode is changed.
Due to the interaction of the electron's electric field and the magnet's magnetic field, the electrons take a curved path from the cathode to anode.
With the application of the correct magnetic force from the magnet and the correct voltage on the anode, the electrons actually do not reach the anode.
The electrons take a curved path back to the cathode where they are re-emitted.
Due to placement and positioning, the energy of the electrons is coupled to the cavity resonators.
The energy excites the cavity resonators, and oscillations result.
The magnetron can be tuned by varying the size of the cavity resonators with tuning slugs.
As in the klystron, interelectrode capacitance is reduced by the spacing between the cathode and anode.
Lead inductance is reduced by keeping the lengths of internal leads to minimum.
Transit time is of no importance since the output is taken from a cavity resonator.

2. Interelectrode capacitance is caused by the elements in the tube. At high frequencies the reactance can ground signals and cause feedback.
3. Lead inductance is caused by the conductors in the tube acting as inductors. At high frequencies, the reactances attenuate input and output signals.
4. Transit time is the time for electrons to travel from the cathode to the plate. At high frequencies, the time causes phase shifts and power losses.
5. Combining the effects of high frequencies in conventional tubes makes the tubes inefficient for microwave use.
